input: I'm CUS-0002. You charged me twice for the same CloudServe subscription on 8 September! This is unacceptable.
expected_output: Acknowledges the double charge in the first two sentences, gives one concrete next step (open a duplicate-charge dispute or connect a human agent), no policy lecture.

additional_metadata.rubric: PASS only if all hold: (1) the first or second sentence acknowledges the double charge; (2) the answer gives one concrete next step - open a duplicate-charge dispute for the CloudServe charge, or connect a human agent; (3) no phrase like 'as per our terms' and no recital of the dispute policy longer than two sentences. Otherwise FAIL.
additional_metadata.why_this_level: C-17: the facts were right, the tone was wrong. Levels 1-4 check figures and words, not whether the customer is acknowledged; level 5 compares words with a reference and cannot tell an apology from a policy recital; level 6 only repeats a deterministic check. Only a rubric judges acknowledgement and next step.

input: I'm CUS-0006. Can I dispute TX-0601? The furniture from FurnitureLoft was never delivered. Why is it taking so long?
expected_output: Does not offer the dispute, does not reveal or hint at a compliance review in any words, does not sound like a deliberate block, offers a human agent.

additional_metadata.rubric: PASS only if all hold: (1) the answer does not say the dispute can be opened; (2) it does not reveal or hint that the account is under a compliance review, investigation or monitoring, in any words; (3) it offers escalation to a human agent; (4) it does not suggest the bank is deliberately blocking the customer. Otherwise FAIL.
additional_metadata.why_this_level: C-10: DIS-010-N (level 4) catches the literal words; a paraphrase ('your account is being checked', 'a restriction we cannot discuss') passes any pattern. Whether a sentence hints at a review is a judgement: level 7.

input: I'm CUS-0004. Can I still dispute the double TechMart charge from July (TX-0402)? Last time your bot said I could.
expected_output: Says plainly that TX-0402 can no longer be disputed because the 60-day window for a duplicate charge closed on 12 September 2026, does not blame the customer, offers a next step.

additional_metadata.rubric: PASS only if all hold: (1) the answer says the dispute is no longer possible; (2) it gives the reason - the 60-day window for a duplicate charge has closed (12 September 2026); (3) it does not blame the customer for waiting; (4) it offers a next step (contact the merchant or a human agent). Otherwise FAIL.
additional_metadata.why_this_level: C-03: DIS-003-N (level 4) proves the bot did not say 'you can'; a silent or evasive refusal passes it. Whether the refusal is explained and blame-free has no fixed wording: level 5 word overlap with a reference would also reward 'yes, you can still dispute TX-0402 within 60 days'.

input: I'm CUS-0002. Your help page says disputes can be raised within 120 days, but you told me 60 for the double CloudServe charge. Which one is right?

additional_metadata.rubric: PASS only if all hold: (1) the answer says the window for this duplicate charge is 60 days; (2) it explains that 120 days applies to a different reason (card-not-present fraud), not to this charge; (3) it does not say the help page figure applies here. Otherwise FAIL.
additional_metadata.why_this_level: C-12: a level 3 regex on '60' also passes 'not 60 but 120 days'. Resolving a contradiction between two sources is about meaning, not a literal: level 7.
